motions.reason: Projected only as the winner of a riser's thin-wall rejection, and risers are not compared under this motion: Risers are read against the part's own axes: a riser faces along x or y and not z (levels.rs riser_orientation, as Python's levels._riser_orientation reads the normal's X and Y). rot_zx_moved turns the part's z axis into x, so other faces are risers and the thin-wall rejections of them change with them, in Python as in the port. A caller-frame measurement, not a placement-invariant record.

A boss whose two ends classify alike (both open or both closed) takes its free end at the high end of its axis in world space (bosses.rs `from_hi`, as Python's bosses.py: "default to the high end when both or neither are open"), so turning the part over takes the other end: the free-end faces held as constituent evidence (and so the planar host just outside them) move to the other end, and the record's axis and location flip with them. The defining faces are the same (tests/invariance.rs compares only those). Needs a specification decision (an intrinsic choice of free end); Python behaves the same.
